transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Well, I guess what brought me in is... things have been getting really weird at the shop. I'm a mechanic, and lately I keep hearing this man’s voice coming from the garage vents. And it's an older building, you know, cinderblock walls, and the HVAC system is a total joke. We had a guy out to look at the compressor last month because it was whining so bad, sounded exactly like a failing power steering pump on an early 2000s Honda. People always ignore that noise until the whole steering rack is completely shot, which is just throwing money away. 

But... anyway, it's not the compressor. It's a man's voice. Clear as day, like somebody is standing right next to me in the bay. Sometimes it even comes from under the hood of the cars I'm working on. And he just keeps telling me not to trust my husband. Which is... I mean, my husband and I met back when I was taking some classes at the community college. We were in this business management course because I thought about opening my own garage someday. The overhead on commercial leases right now is just completely out of control though, so I don't know if that'll ever happen. 

But yeah, the voice is telling me not to trust him, and it tells me not to touch certain cars at work. So I just... I don't know what to do.
Have you heard this voice anywhere else besides the garage or when you're working on cars?

No, I don't think so... just at the shop. But you know, it's funny you ask about hearing things in other places because my husband and I were just at the grocery store the other day. The big one on 4th street, not the little one by our house. And they have this entire aisle dedicated just to different kinds of sparkling water now. I mean, who needs forty different flavors of bubbly water? Back when I was a kid, you had regular water or you had soda, and that was it. My dad used to drink those generic colas that came in the huge plastic bottles that would go flat after two days. He was always trying to save a buck, which I get, but man, that stuff tasted like battery acid. 

Anyway... where was I? Oh, right. No, the voice is just at the garage. It's weird, right?
Have you noticed any other unusual sensory experiences, like seeing things that aren't there, feeling something on your skin, or smelling odd odors that others don't notice?

No, I haven't seen anything or smelled anything weird. It's really just the voice. Like I said, it's this man's voice coming from the vents at the shop, or sometimes right from under the hood of a car I'm working on. It's so clear, just like you and me talking right now. And he just keeps repeating it, telling me not to trust my husband, and warning me not to touch certain cars. 

Which is really frustrating because we had this 2018 Subaru Forester come in yesterday, and those boxer engines are notoriously tricky if you don't know what you're doing. A lot of guys hate changing the spark plugs on them because there's barely any clearance between the valve cover and the frame rail. You practically need double-jointed fingers and a special swivel socket just to get in there. My old boss, Gary, used to make the new guys do it just to watch them struggle. Gary was a piece of work. He used to smoke these awful cigars right in the office, and the smell would just seep into everything. My work jackets smelled like cheap tobacco for years, even after I washed them a dozen times. 

But yeah, I haven't smelled anything like that lately, or seen anything. Just the voice telling me about my husband and the cars.
Has this kind of thing ever happened to you before, where you heard a voice or felt warned about something in a similar way?

Well, the voice and... the feeling that I'm being warned or tracked or whatever, it's been going on for about ten months now. Ten months of this guy just talking to me at work. Which is crazy because ten months ago was right around the time we had that massive snowstorm. Do you remember that? It dumped like two feet overnight, and the city completely ran out of road salt. People were abandoning their cars on the highway, and our shop was slammed for weeks with people who slid into curbs and destroyed their suspension. I must have replaced twenty tie rods that month alone. It’s always the same thing—people think because they have all-wheel drive, they can just fly down an icy road at sixty miles an hour. All-wheel drive helps you go, it doesn't help you stop. My husband actually got stuck at his office that night and had to sleep under his desk because the plows didn't come through until morning. 

But yeah, it's been about ten months since all this started.
Have you ever had a time when you were experiencing these voices or warnings without also feeling unusually low or high in mood?

Yeah, actually... there was a time like that. A few weeks where things were just really quiet for me. I was sleeping a lot more than usual and I wasn't really making any huge plans or anything. Just kind of laying low, you know? But even then, during that whole quiet stretch, I still heard the garage voice. And I still fully believed my husband and my boss were tracking me. 

Speaking of my boss, he actually installed these new security cameras at the shop around that time. He claimed it was because someone was stealing catalytic converters out of the lot next door. Which, to be fair, is a huge problem right now. People just slide under a truck with a Sawzall and cut them out in two minutes flat. The scrap yards pay good money for the precious metals inside them, like platinum and palladium. We had a guy come in with a Honda Element, and his car sounded like a tractor because somebody chopped his exhaust right in half while he was watching a movie at the AMC. Can you imagine coming out of a nice movie and you turn the key and your car sounds like a Harley Davidson? He was so mad. The replacement part was on backorder for three months, too. The supply chain for parts is just a complete nightmare right now. You can't get anything. We've had a Chevy Silverado sitting on one of our lifts for a week just waiting on a basic brake caliper. 

Wait, what did you ask me? Oh, right, my mood. But yeah, even when I was just quiet and sleeping all the time, the voice and the tracking stuff was still happening.
Have there been any periods in your life when you felt unusually energetic, needed less sleep, or had racing thoughts, even for just a few days?

Yeah, definitely. I mean, sometimes I get this crazy burst of energy where I just can't stop. Like, I won't even need to sleep. When I get going like that, I'll stay at the shop way past closing time. I'll start tearing down three different engines at once, and then I'll decide I need to reorganize all the parts shelves because nobody ever puts the 10-millimeter sockets back where they belong. Why is it always the 10-millimeter? It's like a universal law of mechanics—if you drop a 10-millimeter socket, it enters another dimension. You can buy a pack of ten of them and by the end of the week, they're all gone. 

Anyway, I'll be doing all that, and I'll also be trying to plan a big meet-up for this local car club I'm in. We usually do these Sunday morning drives up through the canyon, which is beautiful in the fall when the leaves change. You get all these classic muscle cars out there, like old Chevelles and GTOs. The sound of a carbureted V8 echoing off the canyon walls is just... there's nothing like it. But you really have to watch out for the cyclists up there. They ride right on the white line, and half the time they don't even look over their shoulder before they swerve into the lane. It's so dangerous. My buddy actually clipped a guy's mirror once because the cyclist just cut right in front of him.

But yeah, even after doing all that—the shop, the cars, the club planning—I still feel like I just have to keep moving, you know? Like my brain is just going a million miles an hour and I can't shut it off.
Have you ever had a period of time when you felt down or depressed for most of the day, nearly every day, and lost interest in things you usually enjoy, even for just a couple of weeks?

No, I don't really think so. I mean, I'm not really a sad person, you know? Even when things are stressful, I don't just sit around feeling down all day. I always have to be doing something. Like, if I'm not at the shop, I'm usually at home working on my own car. I've got this '98 Jeep Cherokee that I've been slowly rebuilding for the last three years. The inline-six engine in those things is basically bulletproof, but the body rusts out if you just look at it wrong. I had to weld in completely new floor pans last summer because the old ones were basically Swiss cheese. You could literally see the driveway through the floorboard on the passenger side. 

My husband hated it because the welding sparks kept burning little holes in his favorite pair of work boots. I told him he shouldn't be wearing soft-toe boots in the garage anyway, right? If you drop a transmission on your foot, a leather boot isn't going to save your toes. You need steel-toe, or at least composite. The composite ones are actually better in the winter because the steel doesn't get freezing cold and turn your feet into ice blocks. 

But no, I don't really get depressed or lose interest in stuff like that. I always have a project going on.

There is no evidence of prominent mood episodes during most of the illness, ruling out F25.2 (schizoaffective disorder, depressive type), F25.8 (other specified schizoaffective disorders), and F25.9 (schizoaffective disorder, unspecified). The presence of a continuous single auditory hallucination without significant mood symptoms supports F25.0 (schizoaffective disorder, unspecified) and possibly F25.1 (schizoaffective disorder, bipolar type) if the mood episodes were present but not dominant. No further hallucinations or delusions in other modalities were reported, and the symptom pattern remains consistent with schizoaffective disorder rather than schizophrenia (F20.0), which would require more pervasive and enduring symptoms.
